sources.snippet: Functional metagenomics showed that bacterial communities from Canadian Arctic permafrost harbored diverse resistance mechanisms at least 5,000 years ago.

sources.title: The Prehistory of Antibiotic Resistance
sources.publisher: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Medicine
sources.snippet: A review describes resistance genes encoding resistance to β-lactam, tetracycline, and glycopeptide antibiotics in 30,000-year-old permafrost metagenomes.

sources.title: Ancient Resistome
sources.snippet: “Antibiotic resistance is an ancient biological mechanism in bacteria, although its proliferation in our contemporary world has been amplified through antimicrobial therapy.”

sources.title: Culturing Ancient Bacteria Carrying Resistance Genes from Permafrost and Comparative Genomics with Modern Isolates
sources.snippet: The study reports that antibiotic resistance mechanisms are much older than human antibiotic use and examines bacteria from a 2.7-million-year-old Siberian permafrost sample.

07-c4.claim: If nothing changes, routine surgery will become impossible within a decade, because the procedures we treat as safe are only safe on the assumption that an infection afterward can be cleared.

sources.title: CONSULTATION DOCUMENT (November 2023): WHO strategic and operational priorities to address drug-resistant bacterial infections, 2025-2035
sources.snippet: WHO states that antimicrobial resistance increases risks that common infections become impossible to treat and routine medical procedures, including surgery, become unsafe.

sources.title: Antimicrobial resistance: accelerating national and global responses
sources.snippet: WHO reports that antimicrobial resistance can make common infections impossible to treat and routine procedures such as surgery unsafe.

sources.title: Confronting antimicrobial resistance 2024 to 2029
sources.publisher: Department of Health and Social Care
sources.snippet: The UK document states that without effective antibiotics, even minor surgery and routine operations could become high-risk if serious infections cannot be treated.
sources.groupAuthor: Department of Health and Social Care

sources.title: The threat of antimicrobial resistance in surgical care: the surgeon’s role and ownership of antimicrobial stewardship
sources.snippet: The article describes surgical-site infections as a major concern and reports that resistant organisms account for a substantial share of infections after gastrointestinal surgery.

08-c1.claim: Ramirez and Doyle (2024) found that students who received AI-generated feedback improved their essay scores by 23 percent over a single semester, a larger effect than any human intervention has produced.

sources.title: Comparing the quality of human and ChatGPT feedback of students’ writing
sources.snippet: “Human raters were better at providing high-quality feedback to students in all categories other than criteria-based.”

sources.title: Automated feedback and writing: a multi-level meta-analysis of effects on students’ performance
sources.snippet: The meta-analysis reports substantial heterogeneity, indicating automated feedback cannot be treated as one consistent intervention.

sources.title: AI-generated feedback on writing: insights into efficacy and ENL student preference
sources.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
sources.snippet: The study examined GPT-4 feedback and student preferences, including pretesting during the first week of a semester.
sources.container: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

sources.title: GPT-4 feedback increases student activation and learning outcomes in higher education
sources.snippet: Over one semester, students answered eight open-ended questions and received lecturer, peer, or AI feedback depending on treatment.

08-c2.claim: Their sample was large and the effect held across grade levels, so the usual complaints about small studies do not apply here.

sources.title: How Does Artificial Intelligence Compare to Human Feedback? A Meta-Analysis of Performance, Feedback Perception, and Learning Dispositions
sources.snippet: The meta-analysis includes separate studies comparing AI feedback with human feedback and studies measuring performance change after feedback interventions.

sources.title: The Effects of AI-Assisted Feedback on Students’ Perceptions, Emotions, and Learning Outcomes in L2 Writing: A Three-Level Meta-Analysis
sources.snippet: The study warns that a substantial effect from a single pilot study highlights an efficacy-effectiveness gap in AI-feedback research.

sources.title: Automated Feedback and Writing: A Multi-Level Meta-Analysis of Effects on Students' Performance
sources.snippet: The meta-analysis examines whether effects of automated writing feedback are moderated by sample, intervention, and outcome characteristics.

sources.title: Can Students Judge Like Experts? A Large-Scale Study on the Pedagogical Quality of AI and Human Personalized Formative Feedback
sources.snippet: The study compares AI-generated and human-authored feedback in higher education using 979 feedback samples and a 472-student user study.

08-c3.claim: GPT-5 class models now score above the median human rater on the AP English Language essay rubric, according to the vendor's own published evaluation.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5
sources.snippet: OpenAI reports GPT-5 evaluation results across capabilities including visual reasoning, agentic coding, and graduate-level scientific problem solving, but the result shown does not mention AP English Language essays.

sources.title: Appendix A Exam Benchmark Methodology
sources.snippet: The methodology says AP English Language and Composition essays were graded by one or two qualified third-party contractors with relevant essay-grading experience.

sources.title: Grading the Graders: Comparing Generative AI and Human Assessment in Essay Evaluation
sources.snippet: The study compares two ChatGPT versions with eight human instructors grading 186 deidentified student essays using a detailed rubric.

sources.title: Comparing GPT and human raters in essay assessment: Variability, bias, and the potential of LLM-based scoring
sources.snippet: The study analyzes ratings by 20 human raters and a GPT-based automated essay-scoring system on 181 university second-language essays using a standardized rubric.

08-c4.claim: Every English teacher I know is quietly worried that AI will grade essays better than they do, and the research says they are right to worry.

sources.title: AI not yet good enough to mark university essays, rewarding ‘style over substance’
sources.snippet: Researchers found AI matched human-awarded degree classifications only around half the time and often rewarded length, vocabulary, and sentence complexity over academic quality.

sources.title: Can AI provide useful holistic essay scoring?
sources.snippet: The study compares minimally prompted language-model scores with trained human ratings and reports that human scoring was generally more reliable, especially for English learners.

sources.title: Can AI grade your essays? A comparative analysis of large language models and teacher ratings in multidimensional essay scoring
sources.snippet: LLM assessment could support teachers, particularly for language-related criteria, but models tended to give higher scores and struggled to capture content quality.

sources.title: Large Language Models in Student Assessment: Comparing ChatGPT and Human Graders
sources.snippet: GPT-4 grades primarily reflected generic language quality and did not reliably adapt to nuanced grading criteria compared with university teachers.

sources.title: EFL teachers’ perceptions of the use of an AI grading tool (CoGrader) in English writing assessment
sources.snippet: The study examines English teachers’ concerns about AI grading and reports that teachers strongly supported maintaining control and receiving training when using such tools.

09-c1.claim: The council voted last year to remove parking minimums for new downtown apartments, and rents have not moved since.

sources.title: Introductions Appropriate To Purpose And Context - AP English Language and Composition
sources.snippet: “the city council is voting on whether to eliminate minimum parking requirements”

sources.title: Parking and the City
sources.snippet: The book discusses removing parking requirements and reports that bundled parking was associated with about $200 more monthly rent for downtown Los Angeles apartments.

sources.title: Introductions Appropriate To Purpose And Context - AP English Language and Composition
sources.snippet: The example frames Riverside's parking-minimum decision as affecting whether new downtown apartments remain affordable or become more expensive for renters.

09-c2.claim: A two-bedroom apartment within walking distance of downtown now lists for more than $2,400 a month, and the vacancy rate downtown has been under two percent for three straight years.

sources.title: Apartments for Rent in Downtown Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA - 416 Rentals in Downtown Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA
sources.snippet: Current Downtown Los Angeles two-bedroom rental listings include asking prices of $2,400 or more per month.

sources.title: Downtown living at its finest! 2 bed 1 bath Apartments - 612&618 N 3rd Street San Jose CA
sources.snippet: Zumper reports a September 2026 median rent of $3,845 for two-bedroom apartments in Downtown San Jose.

sources.title: Market Feasibility Analysis
sources.snippet: The report states that surveyed rental communities had a combined stabilized vacancy rate of 1.8 percent and average two-bedroom market-rate rents of $2,342.

sources.title: Condo Market Report, Fourth Quarter 2017
sources.snippet: The report says condominium vacancy was below one percent in fall 2017 and the average two-bedroom condominium rent was $2,627.

09-c3.claim: Cities that removed parking requirements have seen developers build smaller and cheaper units, and researchers estimate that each structured parking space adds tens of thousands of dollars to the cost of the apartment above it.

sources.title: The Impacts of Minimum Parking Requirements: A Research Synthesis
sources.snippet: Research finds that eliminating parking minimums expands housing options by enabling smaller units and facilitates more affordable cities.

sources.title: No Such Thing as Free Parking: Construction Costs in 17 U.S. Cities
sources.snippet: Required parking can add tens of thousands of dollars per housing unit and sometimes increase total construction costs by more than 50%.

sources.title: Parking policy: The effects of residential minimum parking requirements in Seattle
sources.snippet: The study finds that reducing parking requirements leads to less parking provision, presumed developer cost savings, and lower housing prices for consumers.

sources.title: What Happens When Cities Eliminate Minimum Parking Requirements?
sources.snippet: Evidence from cities removing minimums shows that more affordable units were offered with no on-site parking, while other projects provided larger units and more parking.
